I'll start by reading the spec and the current parser implementation.
Now I have the full picture. Let me implement Q15 in the parser.
Now the leading-word drop list and the trim helper:
Files changed: `app/src/main/java/com/sherifradwan/ancnative/ui/DeliveryNotesParser.kt` (only). ClinicalFormat.kt already satisfied Q5/Q6, so I left it untouched.

Q15(a): added last, previous, prior, earlier, repeat, elective, emergency, CS, LSCS, SVD, NVD to `HOSPITAL_LEADING_WORDS` (whole word, case-insensitive, at least one word always kept). Replaced `dropLeadingWords` with `trimLeadingWords` returning a small `TrimmedPhrase(name, dropped)` so the dropped text is not lost.

Q15(b): `isPreviousDeliveryPhrase(text, phraseStart, dropped)` now evaluates `text-before-phrase + " " + dropped`, so dropped words count as text before the phrase — a dropped "Last CS" acts as a past marker, a dropped "Elective" as a current marker (they land immediately before the phrase, so the "current marker between past marker and phrase" test sees them).

Assumption 1: "Previous LSCS Al Salam Hospital" (test expects null) cannot match the Q13 marker list as written, so I added LSCS/SVD/NVD to `PAST_DELIVERY_MARKER`'s delivery-word group. Effect is only extra skipping of unlabelled phrases after a past marker (a false negative keeps the line verbatim in Plan, per the safety rule); no clinical threshold, wording or testTag touched, no new libraries, parser still a pure function.

All Q1-Q14 behaviour is preserved (I checked each existing hospital/tense example by reading the assertions); the full unit suite is green.
